column3: Close to the Hebrew; וּמוּסָר (“discipline”) is rendered “instruction.”
Close to the Hebrew; “instruction of insight” is rendered “the instruction of wisdom,” and “righteousness, justice, uprightness” “Justice, judgment, and equity.”
Close to the Hebrew; the jussive “let the wise hear” is rendered “A wise man will hear.”
Close to the Hebrew; וְחִידֹתָם (“their riddles”) is rendered “their riddles.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the instruction (torah) of your mother” is rendered “the law of your mother.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a wreath of favor” is rendered “a graceful ornament.”
Close to the Hebrew; “let us lie in wait for blood” is rendered “to shed blood.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV keeps כִּשְׁאוֹל (“like Sheol”) as “like Sheol.”
Close to the Hebrew; “every owner of a wing” is rendered “any bird.”
Close to the Hebrew; “at the head of noisy places” is rendered “in the chief concourses.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV swaps the comparisons, rendering “like devastation” as “like a storm” and “like a storm-wind” as “like a whirlwind.”
